title: Countable & uncountable nouns
grammarNote: ИСЧИСЛЯЕМЫЕ существительные (countable) — предметы, которые можно посчитать: one apple, two apples. У них есть единственное и множественное число. НЕИСЧИСЛЯЕМЫЕ (uncountable) — вещества, понятия, массы: water, milk, rice, advice. У них нет множественного числа и нельзя поставить a/an. Это влияет на выбор артикля, квантора и формы глагола.

grammarTable.subject: Countable singular
grammarTable.example: an apple · a tomato · a café · an egg · a recipe

grammarTable.subject: Uncountable
grammarTable.example: water · milk · rice · bread · sugar · cheese · advice · information

grammarTable.subject: With quantities (C)
grammarTable.example: a few apples · many tomatoes · three eggs · several dishes

grammarTable.subject: With quantities (U)
grammarTable.example: a little water · much sugar · a lot of milk · some rice

grammarTable.subject: Question (C)
grammarTable.example: How many apples? · How many students? · How many dishes?

grammarTable.subject: Question (U)
grammarTable.example: How much water? · How much rice? · How much sugar?

grammarTable.subject: Partitive (U → C)
grammarTable.example: a glass of water · a piece of bread · a kilo of cheese · a cup of tea

rows.form: Liquids: water, milk, juice, tea, coffee, oil, broth
rows.example: "some water" ✅ · "a water" ❌ · "two milks" ❌ · "some milk" ✅

rows.form: Grains: rice, bread, flour, pasta, cereal
rows.example: "some rice" ✅ · "two rices" ❌ · "a bread" ❌ · "a loaf of bread" ✅

rows.form: Other: cheese, butter, sugar, salt, honey, meat
rows.example: "some cheese" ✅ · "a cheese" ❌ · "much sugar" ✅ · "a piece of cheese" ✅
"some advice" ✅ · "an advice" ❌ · "many informations" ❌
a glass of water · a bottle of juice · a cup of coffee
a piece of bread · a slice of cheese · a chunk of meat
a kilo of tomatoes · 500 grams of butter · a litre of milk
a bowl of soup · a plate of beshbarmak · a portion of rice
just a bit of honey · a little sugar · a little milk
"Can I give you a piece of advice?" (not "an advice")

grammarExtra.title: Nouns that can be BOTH countable and uncountable

rows.example: I love coffee. · She drinks too much coffee.
Can I have a coffee? · Two coffees, please!
This beshbarmak has chicken in it.
She bought a chicken at the market.
I need some cheese for the salad.
This is a delicious French cheese.
✅ I need some advice. (advice is always uncountable!)
✅ She gave me two pieces of information.
✅ Can I have some rice? / a portion of rice?
✅ I drank three glasses of water.

grammarTip:
Как определить, исчисляемое ли существительное?
① Можно ли сказать: ONE ___, TWO ___s? → Исчисляемое ✅
   one apple, two apples ✅ · one egg, two eggs ✅
② Звучит ли странно множественное число?
   two waters ❌ · two rices ❌ · two advices ❌ → Неисчисляемое!

💡 Золотое правило с едой:
• Еда как ВЕЩЕСТВО = неисчисляемое: cheese, bread, rice, chicken (meat)
• Еда как ЕДИНИЦА/ПРЕДМЕТ = исчисляемое: a biscuit, two sandwiches, a chicken (bird)

💡 Неисчисляемое → используй партитивные выражения:
a glass OF water · a piece OF bread · a kilo OF cheese · a bowl OF soup

exercises.hint: Rice cannot be counted individually. We say "some rice" or "a bowl of rice".
Bread is uncountable → a piece of bread OR some bread.

exercises.text: "Can I have an advice?" is correct English.
exercises.hint: Advice is uncountable → "Can I have some advice?" or "a piece of advice".

opts: She drank three glasses of water.
exercises.correct: She drank three glasses of water.
exercises.hint: Water is uncountable → three glasses of water.
Cheese as a substance is uncountable. "A cheese" = a type of cheese.

exercises.text: Can I have a ___ of soup? It smells amazing.
exercises.hint: a bowl of soup = the standard partitive expression for soup.

exercises.text: There is ___ milk left in the fridge.
exercises.hint: Milk is uncountable → a little milk (not "a few milk").

exercises.text: Which of these nouns can you say "two ___s"?
exercises.hint: Recipe is countable: one recipe, two recipes ✅. Others are uncountable.

exercises.text: "Two coffees, please!" is correct in English.
exercises.hint: "Two coffees" = two cups of coffee. When used as a serving, coffee is countable! ✅

questions.hint: Water cannot be counted: "a water" ❌, "two waters" ❌ → uncountable.

questions.text: How ___ sugar is in this recipe?

questions.hint: "some bread" ✅ — bread is uncountable → no article, no plural.
"a chicken" = one whole bird (countable). "some chicken" = some meat.

questions.text: "Can I have two rices?" is correct.
questions.hint: Rice is uncountable → "Can I have some rice?" or "two portions of rice?"

questions.text: Which partitive is correct for water?
questions.hint: a glass of water ✅ — standard partitive for liquids.

questions.text: Choose the correct quantity for an uncountable noun.
questions.hint: "a little" is used with uncountable nouns. "a few" is for countable.

questions.text: I need ___ kilo of cheese for the recipe.
questions.hint: "a kilo" = one unit of measurement → "a kilo of cheese".
In a café, "a coffee" = one cup. Two coffees = two cups. ✅
Advice is always uncountable: "some advice" or "a piece of advice". Never "an advice".

questions.text: "___ apples are there?" — correct question for countable.
She gave me a useful ___ of advice.
questions.hint: "a piece of advice" — the standard partitive for uncountable "advice".
Information is always uncountable: "some information" ✅, never plural.

questions.text: Which of these food items is uncountable?
questions.hint: Butter is uncountable (a substance): "some butter" ✅, "a butter" ❌.
